app.title: AURORA
app.subtitle: Frequency Discovery
app.motto: Discover frequencies by data, not by belief.

warnings.exploratory: Exploratory score — not evidence of therapeutic or metaphysical efficacy.
warnings.simulation: This pattern is a mathematical simulation; physical formation is not guaranteed.
warnings.safety: Listen at a safe level with headphones. Amplitude is capped at 0.2. The audible range is 20–20,000 Hz; frequencies outside it are generated but cannot be heard.
warnings.blind: The real frequency of a condition stays hidden until the study ends.
warnings.multiple: Multiple comparisons: Bonferroni applied for {{k}} comparisons.
warnings.noClaim: AURORA never labels a frequency as 'healing'; it only shows measured properties.
warnings.inaudibleBand: This frequency lies outside human hearing — it is generated and analysed, but you will not hear it.
warnings.notRenderableHint: The device sample rate cannot render this frequency (Nyquist limit: half the sample rate).

home.title: AURORA FREQUENCY
home.stackHint: You can play several frequencies at once — stacked together they sound like a chord.
home.simpleHint: Type the frequencies you want (or pick below), then press Play. They all sound at once. Tap a row to analyse that frequency.
home.spectrumMulti: All of them show in the spectrum: {{list}} Hz
home.randomHint: Truly random — nothing is picked from a list; a decimal number is generated. You choose how many and in what range.
home.seedNote: New numbers each time you press; they cannot be repeated.

library.title: Candidate Library
library.corpusIntro: Every number is stored with where it came from. Ancient texts contain numbers, not hertz — any conversion to frequency is always tagged 'derived'.
library.wrongEntryHelp: If the evidence level or citation is off, report it on GitHub — a correction is a real contribution.

experiment.title: Blind Experiment
experiment.noStudy: No active study. Start one from Setup.
experiment.underpowered: Underpowered — this design cannot support a 'no effect' conclusion. Increase repetitions or reduce conditions.

journal.title: 30-Day Journal
journal.moodHelp: Set the sliders to match today. There is no right answer — just how you were.
journal.countsHelp: Count the countable things. This is the only way to turn 'my luck changed' into something measurable: events, not feelings.
journal.listenedHelp: Pick a protocol if you listened to one. Leave it as 'None' if you did not — empty days are data too.
journal.noEntries: No entries yet. Fill in your first day and the chart appears here.
journal.exportHelp: All your records in one file. Keep it as a backup or send it to someone.
journal.importHelp: Pick an AURORA file someone sent you. Nothing of yours is deleted — only new records are added.
journal.importOverwrite: Overwrite if the same record exists
journal.importNothing: Nothing new — you already have all of it.
journal.errInvalidJson: This file is damaged or not JSON.
journal.errNotAuroraFile: This is not an AURORA file.
journal.errNewerVersion: This file comes from a newer version. Please update the app.

lab.title: Lab
lab.plateWarning: A Chladni pattern depends on the PLATE, not the frequency. Enter the parameters of your real setup below — the pattern is computed from them.
lab.offResonance: This frequency is far from the plate's resonance — real sand may not form a clear pattern.

glossary.amplitude: How loud the sound is. 0 = silent, 0.2 = safe maximum. It does not change the pitch, only the intensity.
glossary.frequency: Vibrations per second (Hz). Higher Hz = higher pitch. 440 Hz is the orchestra's tuning 'A'.
glossary.waveform: The shape of the wave. A sine is the purest tone (one frequency); square/saw add harmonics and sound harsher.
glossary.cent: A fine unit of pitch. 100 cents = 1 semitone, 1200 cents = 1 octave. The ear can tell about 5-8 cents apart.
glossary.harmonic: Whole multiples of the base frequency (2x, 3x, 4x...). Present in all natural sounds; they give a sound its colour.
glossary.octave: Double the frequency. 432 Hz and 864 Hz are the same note one octave apart, and the ear hears them as 'the same'.
glossary.octaveClass: What is left of a frequency once octave differences are ignored. 432, 864 and 216 share one octave class.
glossary.ratio: The ratio between two frequencies. Simple ones like 3:2 (fifth) and 4:3 (fourth) sound consonant - Pythagoras' discovery.
glossary.digitalRoot: Digits summed until one remains. 528 → 5+2+8=15 → 1+5=6. Used in numerology; it has no physical meaning.
glossary.prime: A number divisible only by 1 and itself. A mathematical property with no acoustic consequence.
glossary.chladni: The pattern sand forms on a vibrating plate. Sand gathers along the 'nodal lines' where the plate does not move.
glossary.node: A point or line where vibration is zero. Sand collects exactly there.
glossary.resonance: The plate's own natural frequency. Driven at it, the pattern is strongest and sharpest.
glossary.mode: (m,n) - the number of waves across and down the pattern. Every resonance has its own mode.
glossary.plateEffect: A Chladni pattern depends on the PLATE, not the frequency alone. The same 528 Hz gives a different pattern on different material, size or thickness.
glossary.symmetry: Mirror symmetry of the pattern (0-1). 1 means perfectly symmetric.
glossary.complexity: Density of lines in the pattern (0-1). Higher frequencies produce more complex patterns.
glossary.spectrum: The distribution of frequencies inside a sound - which ones are present and how strong.
glossary.fft: Fourier transform - the maths that splits a sound into the pure frequencies it contains.
glossary.infrasound: Below 20 Hz - inaudible, sometimes felt as vibration. Ordinary speakers cannot reproduce it.
glossary.ultrasound: Above 20,000 Hz - beyond human hearing. Bats and dogs hear it.
glossary.nyquist: To render a tone, the sample rate must be at least twice its frequency. On a 48 kHz device the ceiling is 24 kHz.
glossary.layer: One of the frequencies playing at the same time. Stacked together they form a chord-like structure.
glossary.blinding: Not knowing which frequency you are hearing, so expectation cannot shape the result.
glossary.preregistration: Writing down what you will measure BEFORE collecting data, so the rules cannot be changed to fit the result.
glossary.primaryOutcome: The single question the study is really answering. Chosen up front and never changed afterwards.
glossary.cohenD: Effect size. 0.2 small, 0.5 medium, 0.8 large. More informative than a p-value.
glossary.pValue: The probability the result is chance. A small p means chance is unlikely - but it is not proof on its own.
glossary.confidenceInterval: The 95% range the true value most likely falls in. If it includes zero, the effect is uncertain.
glossary.bonferroni: A multiple-comparison correction. Test ten things and one looks 'significant' by luck; this guards against that.
glossary.power: The chance of detecting an effect that really exists. Below 80% is considered inadequate.
glossary.mde: Minimum detectable effect. Anything smaller cannot be seen with this sample size.
glossary.randomization: Shuffling the order of conditions, so effects like 'the first one felt better' cancel out.
glossary.control: The comparison condition (usually silence). Without it, calling something 'effective' is impossible.
glossary.evidenceLevel: How firmly a claim rests on a source: DIRECT (stated in the text) through to SPECULATIVE (a modern claim).
glossary.exploratoryScore: How mathematically or historically interesting a frequency is. It does NOT mean the frequency works.
glossary.dtw: An alignment method that compares two frequency sequences even when they run at different speeds.
glossary.simulation: A computer model, not a real measurement. There is no guarantee physics will match it.
